chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Maskan from Abu Hamzah from Yahya ibn Aqil from Habashi who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) addressed the people, praised Allah and glorified Him, and mentioned his cousin Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and sent blessings upon him.

Then he said: 'Now then, verily those who came before you were destroyed due to the sins they committed while their rabbis and scholars did not forbid them from that. When they became excessive in sins, punishments descended upon them.'
So enjoin good and forbid evil, and know that enjoining good and forbidding evil neither bring death closer nor do they sever [one's] livelihood.
Indeed, the [divine] command descends from the sky to the earth like drops of rain; to every individual [comes] what is ordained by Allah to increase or decrease.
So if any of you is afflicted by a calamity in his family, wealth, or self, and sees a punishment [upon] his brother, let it not be an ordeal for him; he awaits one of two good outcomes.

Either a caller from Allah [in the form of death], in which case what is with Allah is better for him, or sustenance from Allah. If he possesses family, wealth, or children, that is the tillage of this world, and good deeds are the tillage of the Hereafter, and Allah may gather both for some groups.

key_terms.الْأَحْبَارُ: Al-Ahbar: Jewish scholars or learned men
key_terms.الْحَسَنَان: Al-Hasanayn: The two good outcomes (death or sustenance)
key_terms.لِحَرْثِ الدُّنْيَا: Li-harthi al-dunya: For the tillage/cultivation of the world
key_terms.لِحَرْثِ الْآخِرَةِ: Li-harthi al-akhira: For the tillage/cultivation of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of enjoining good and forbidding evil in Shia tradition according to Imam Ali's sermon?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the societal decay of previous nations to the complacency of their scholars (Rabbaniyyun), emphasizing that enjoining good and forbidding evil is a communal obligation that does not diminish one's lifespan or sustenance, as divine decree (Qadr) governs all outcomes. He further contextualizes worldly wealth and progeny as temporary means for the hereafter, encouraging believers to view death or continued life as a blessing depending on whether one is actively calling to Allah or enjoying His provisions.
